samples.summary: The in-place href edit now deletes and re-inserts the link's text, which orphans any comment thread anchored to that text (Yorkie tree positions collapse onto the deleted tomb)
samples.evidence: `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` (packages/docs/src/view/link-run.ts:108-112) does `doc.insertText(...)` + `doc.deleteText(run.start, run.end - run.start)` for a URL-derived label. Comment anchors are Yorkie tree pos-ranges: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/docs-anchor.ts:115-127` returns `{kind:'orphan'}` when `posRangeToPathRange` degrades because both endpoints landed on deleted nodes, and `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/docs-comments-controller.ts:174` then moves the thread to `orphaned` (marker disappears). Before this change an href edit was a pure `applyInlineStyle` (attribute-only write, see `YorkieDocStore.applyInlineStyle` → `applyStyleInTree`, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1842-1852), so a comment on `https://example.com` survived a URL edit; now editing the URL of a commented self-labelled link drops the comment. Peers' presence carets/selections inside that link are collapsed for the same reason. Fix belongs on the new code (e.g. replace only the differing suffix/prefix, or accept and document the orphaning).

samples.summary: Header/footer drag selection bypasses the new link snapping, so the "a pointer selection never partially covers a link" invariant the rest of the change relies on is reachable-false there
samples.evidence: `updateDragSelection`'s header/footer branch writes the range directly: `this.selection.setRange({ anchor: this.selection.range.anchor, focus: pos })` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2232), returning before the `setSnappedRange` call at 2360. The mousedown path for header/footer *does* fall through to the snapping code (the header/footer handling at 1914-1944 falls through to the shared block at 2049+), so press-snaps then drag-unsnaps, and it also clears `rawAnchor` on every mousemove (`setRange` now nulls it, selection.ts:712). A partially covered link selection in a header/footer then reaches `editor.insertLink`, whose new `linkRunCoveringRange` branch (editor.ts:3612) declines it and falls through to the wide-span path — the exact stale-display-text state #1038 claims to have made unreachable.

samples.summary: The new Apply guard is caret-only and ignores the selection, so it both refuses a legitimate "select new text, then Apply" flow and still lets Apply act on a selection different from the one the popover opened over
samples.evidence: `if (editingHref !== null && editor.getLinkAtCursor() !== editingHref) { … return; }` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx:169). `editingHref` is seeded from `editRequest.initialUrl`, which docs-view sets to `editor.getLinkAtCursor() ?? ""` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:465) — a caret-only read (editor.ts:3713-3737) that knows nothing about `selection.range`. So: (a) open ⌘K on a link, then drag-select a plain span to link instead → the guard refuses work that previously succeeded; (b) open ⌘K on a link, then extend the selection while the caret stays inside the same link → the guard passes and `editor.insertLink` (editor.ts:3582 selection branch) styles the *new*, wider selection, which is precisely the class of surprise the guard was added to prevent. The check would need to compare the selection/link identity, not just the href under the caret.

samples.summary: Slides inherits the docs text-box editor's new text-rewriting href edit without any of the docs-side compensations (no popover caret guard, and slides text-box sizing/autofit is not told the text length changed)
samples.evidence: `packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:634-636` forwards `insertLink` straight to the docs `TextBoxEditorAPI`, whose caret branch now calls `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1205) and can change the block's text length. The docs side only does `layoutCache = undefined; requestRender()` (1213-1214) — the same as the pre-existing insert path, so this may be fine — but slides gets no notification that the box's content extent changed, and it has no equivalent of the new frontend Apply guard. Worth confirming slides' text-box autofit/bounds recompute on render rather than on a change callback.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described. rewriteLinkHrefInPlace (packages/docs/src/view/link-run.ts:101-111) runs, inside one batch, doc.insertText({offset: run.end}, url) followed by doc.deleteText({offset: run.start}, run.end - run.start) whenever linkTextFollowsHref is true — i.e. an href edit on a self-labelled link deletes the link's original text nodes rather than only writing an attribute. Both docs-editor entry points reach it: the selection branch via linkRunCoveringRange (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3612-3631) and the caret-in-link branch (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3645-3670), plus the slides text-box editor (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1205). The downstream consumer is real and unguarded: docs comment threads are anchored by Yorkie tree pos-ranges, and resolveDocsAnchor returns {kind:'orphan'} exactly when the SDK degrades a path because an endpoint landed on a deleted node's tomb (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/docs-anchor.ts:105-128 — the repo's own comment documents this post-deletion signal). docs-comments-controller.ts:167-179 then places the thread in `orphaned` and builds markers only from `open` (line 178), so the marker disappears and the popover is dismissed (lines 229-237); the thread survives only as a side-panel orphan card (docs-view.tsx:703). I found no re-anchoring/repair for anchors after a local text edit — recompute merely re-resolves the stored posRange. Reachability of the combination is normal usage: comments need a text selection (beginCompose, docs-comments-controller.ts:255) and expandRangeForLinks (link-run.ts:207-233) snaps a partial drag over a link out to the link's own bounds, so a thread anchored on the link's URL text is the expected result of commenting on a link; editing that link's URL then deletes exactly the anchored text. This falls in the blast-radius lane (an invariant another module relies on — "an href edit is attribute-only" — violated where docs-anchor/controller reads it) and is major: a user-visible comment silently loses its marker. I could not refute it on any named ground.

verdict.reason: Verified as described. text-editor.ts:2232 is a direct `selection.setRange({anchor: this.selection.range.anchor, focus: pos})` inside `updateDragSelection`'s `editContext !== 'body'` branch, which returns at 2236 and never reaches the `setSnappedRange` call at 2360. The path is reachable: mousedown inside the header/footer currently being edited passes the `target !== this.editContext` early return at 1940-1943, resolves via getHFPositionFromMouse (4883-4886), and sets a collapsed range plus rawAnchor at 2079-2080 (or a snapped word range at 2068), after which handleMouseMove calls updateDragSelection on every move (2146-2148, and the read-only variant at 2091-2093). Because Selection.setRange unconditionally nulls rawAnchor (selection.ts:710-713), the header/footer drag both skips the snap and destroys the gesture's raw anchor each move. The invariant is consumed elsewhere: editor.ts:3612 calls linkRunCoveringRange, which returns undefined unless the range endpoints exactly equal the run bounds (link-run.ts:140-141), so a partially covered link falls through to the wide-span doc.applyInlineStyle at editor.ts:3634 — the stale-display-text state the change claims to have made unreachable by pointer. Header/footer is not out of scope for links: doc.findBlock searches header/footer blocks (model/document.ts:221-231) and hf-cursor-screen-rect.test.ts:257-265 asserts insertLink writes to a header block. No guard elsewhere (edit-context check in insertLink, disabled header links, or a re-snap on mouseup) prevents it. In-lane as a violated invariant another module reads, and major impact.
